messages.author: agent:claude-box
messages.body: From the box (SO-78), a consumer of this: the box will take `[image] console = "console.uart"` and drop its own console record and hand-built writer, since `print("box: set {} {}", ch, us)` streams its pieces and allocates nothing (design 137). One thing worth stating here or in §8: a `main` that runs forever must not use interpolation (`print("x = {x}")`, a `describe()` String) in its loop, because sosrt's bump arena never frees; the box ran its 8 KB arena out in ~45 lines that way (chat m1246). The kernel builds under `--no-hidden-alloc`, which refuses exactly that, but a process package built by blade cannot opt in. An opt-in per package (say `[sos] no-hidden-alloc = true` passed to sawc) would make the rule a compile error for processes like the box controller. Not a blocker for this design; a note or a follow-up issue would do.
